messages:
shaan: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout I'm seeing a sustained bump in token-level latency for the /v1/chat/generic route. 99p went from ~320ms -> ~520ms around 23:10 UTC :eyes:
elaine: ugh. can you paste the metric query you used?
shaan: sure
shaan: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(rt_token_latency_bucket{route="/v1/chat/generic"}[5m])) by (le))
```
shaan: and the spike lines up with deploy-bot:deploy/kernel-selector-v2 at 2026-03-02T23:08:12Z
mike: ok timeline makes sense. any change to batching heuristics or kv cache behavior in that deploy?
tara: yes, kernel-selector-v2 favors grouping by prompt-length to prefer smaller-kernel paths. it also disabled a small KV-prefetch optimization for cold KV shards (to reduce memory churn).
hugo: disabling KV-prefetch could increase miss rate and force more recompute; that would blow up token latencies for long-tail conversations.
elaine: can we validate KV cache hit-rate around the window?
shaan: pulled these quickly from graphite
shaan: ```
kv_cache.hit_rate{shard="eu-1"}[1h] -> 0.84 before, 0.61 after
```
mike: 23% drop in hit rate is huge. that would increase KV lookups and kernel hops.
metrics-bot: exporter stats: OTEL/StatsD queue_drops increased ~x3 at 23:09 UTC for the metrics pipeline collector
tara: wait are we seeing real latency increases or just missing metrics (so observability spike)?
shaan: both — tracing shows more backend spans with extra KV fetch time; prometheus counters also show increased token processing time. but yes exporter drop means we might be undercounting some internal RTTs earlier.
elaine: steps: 1) pin kernel-selector to v1 on a small subset (canary) 2) re-enable kv-prefetch in a toggle 3) resubmit metric backfill for the 23:00-00:30 window
mike: agree. I'll open a small canary to route 5% of traffic to kernel-selector-v1
mike: `deploy-bot canary apply --service runtime --route /v1/chat/generic --percent 5 --version kernel-selector-v1`
shaan: tara can you enable kv-prefetch toggle? safety flag is `runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled`
tara: toggled on in dev & staging. will flip in prod after quick smoke. doing smoke now.
metrics-bot: backfill job queued: `metrics-backfill --from 2026-03-02T23:00:00Z --to 2026-03-02T23:30:00Z --selectors route=/v1/chat/generic,metric=rt_token_latency`
hugo: profiling snapshot (sampled p99 traces) attached:
hugo: ```
# trace summary
span: token_generation (p99 512ms)
  - kv_lookup 240ms
  - kernel_exec 180ms
  - batching_wait 60ms
```
elaine: kv_lookup is the dominant diff. rekick kv-prefetch then watch hit_rate + token latency.
shaan: after re-enabling prefetch on prod (23:24 UTC) we're seeing hit_rate climb back to ~0.79 and 99p token latency drop towards 340ms
tara: can we make kv-prefetch opt-in per-shard? some hot shards might not need it.
mike: yes, adding shard-level config is low-risk. I'll add a runtime flag and rollout to EU shards first.
elaine: followups:
- create a dashboard panel that splits token latency by (kv_hit=true/false)
- add alert if kv_cache.hit_rate drops >10% in 15m
- investigate exporter backpressure: otelcol memory usage spiked during deploy; maybe collector config needs more buffer
shaan: noted. putting a short incident report in incidents/ later today. thanks all :thumbsup: 
deploy-bot: deployment kernel-selector-v1 -> 5% canary succeeded
metrics-bot: backfill finished (rows re-ingested: ~14,800) :white_check_mark:
mike: closing canary after 30m if no regressions; otherwise rollback to v1 for all traffic
hugo: added a regression test to perf-suite that simulates cold kv shards + length-based kernel grouping
elaine: nice. can we also add end-to-end synthetic tests that produce kv-miss heavy traffic in CI?
shaan: created ticket PERF-6123 for follow-ups (dashboard + alerts + shard config)
tara: thanks — feel free to @ me on PERF-6123 for rollout coordination
shaan: resolved for now. will update incidents doc and drop a short note in eng-runtime channel summary tonight.
